submission.notes: SOLO, to price laterality normalisation on the leaderboard. Every left knee is mirrored so all studies face the same way; the axis is chosen PER PLANE - sagittal reverses SLICE ORDER, coronal and axial reverse WIDTH - because on a sagittal view the medial-lateral direction IS the slice axis. The first attempt at this run flipped width everywhere and corrupted half the input. The comparison is against the parent convnext_base_25d_18slices: val 0.9008 vs 0.9010 (-0.0002), LB 0.914 for the parent. Per finding the six side-dependent findings move -0.0011 on average and the other six +0.0007, so normalisation makes the findings it targets slightly WORSE. Submitted because val has under-called this family before: convnext_base_25d_perfinding_slots_and_pooling was 0.0049 below its parent on val and beat it on the leaderboard, 0.915 vs 0.914. At inference the side comes from the DICOM headers (mean x of ImagePositionPatient) rather than data/12_laterality.csv, which the hidden test set has no entry in; checks/laterality_run_check.py proves that rule reproduces the CSV on 4407/4407 studies, and a study with no readable x is left unflipped. SCORED 0.919. That is the HIGHEST single-run public score this project has recorded, above convnext_base_relabel's 0.918 and its own parent convnext_base_25d_18slices' 0.914. Validation had called it -0.0002 against that parent, so the leaderboard disagrees by about +0.005. This is the SECOND consecutive member of the 2.5D family that val under-called: convnext_base_25d_perfinding_slots_and_pooling was 0.0049 below its parent on val and beat it 0.915 to 0.914. Caveat: the public split is a fraction of ~1300 studies, so a single 0.005 gap is not far outside its own noise - but the DIRECTION has now been wrong twice, which a coin flip explains less well.
